title: Придаточные 3–5: whose, whom, where; дополнительная информация; -ing/-ed clauses
summary: Научимся говорить «у которого», «где», «в тот день, когда», отличать уточнение от «кстати» с запятыми (my brother, who lives in Berlin), строить all of whom и , which surprised everyone — и сжимать придаточные до the guy talking to Tom и the game made by two people.

grammar.title: 1. Главная идея: «какой именно» или «кстати, …»
grammar.html:
Что вы уже знаете (урок B1-21): who / that / which склеивают две фразы, «который» можно выбросить (the game I bought), а предлог уходит в конец (the guy I work with). Теперь главное открытие B2: придаточные бывают двух типов. Первый отвечает на вопрос «какой именно?». Второй просто добавляет информацию — «кстати, …». По-русски запятая стоит всегда, а в английском именно запятая показывает тип.
Русский

Женщина, которая живёт по соседству, — врач.

Мой брат Бен, который живёт в Гонконге, — архитектор.

Обе фразы с запятыми.

English

The woman who lives next door is a doctor. — какая именно? Без запятых.

My brother Ben, who lives in Hong Kong, is an architect. — и так ясно, кто; просто добавка. С запятыми.

Придаточное с запятыми можно вырезать — и фраза не потеряет смысла: My brother Ben is an architect. Первый тип вырезать нельзя: The woman is a doctor — какая женщина?

grammar.title: 2. whose — «чей», «у которого»
grammar.html:
whose заменяет his, her, their, its в придаточном. По-русски это «у которого», «чей», «которого (кого-то)». После whose всегда идёт существительное.
Две фразыОдна фраза
We helped some people. Their car had broken down.We helped some people whose car had broken down.
I follow a streamer. His cat always sits on the keyboard.I follow a streamer whose cat always sits on the keyboard.
I met a girl. I went to school with her brother.I met a girl whose brother I went to school with.

Сравните who и whose:

  • I met a man who knows you. — …который знает тебя. (он знает)
  • I met a man whose sister knows you. — …сестра которого знает тебя. (его сестра знает)

whose можно и для компаний, стран, вещей: It's a studio whose games are all about cats. — Это студия, все игры которой — про котов.

I have a friend who's brother is a pilot.
I have a friend whose brother is a pilot.

who's звучит так же, но это who is / who has: I have a friend who's learning Korean. I have a friend who's just moved to Seoul.

A designer whose his work I love.
A designer whose work I love. — whose уже значит «его»

grammar.title: 3. whom, where, the day, the reason
grammar.html:
whom — «которого, которому» (когда человек — дополнение). Это официально: письма, статьи, новости. В разговоре говорят who или вообще ничего:

ОфициальноВ жизни
a person whom I admirea person I admire
friends with whom you can relaxfriends you can relax with

where — для места, «где, в котором»:

  • I went back to the town where I grew up. — Я вернулся в город, где вырос.
  • The café where we met has closed. — Кафе, где мы познакомились, закрылось.
  • I'd love to live somewhere where it's warm all year.
The city where I visited last year.
The city (that) I visited last year. — visit что? город; «где» тут нет
Проверка: если внутри можно сказать there (I grew up there) — ставьте where. Если там it (I visited it) — that / which или ничего.

the day, the time, the year — обычно без слова: That's the day I'm flying to Oslo. The last time I saw her, she had blue hair. Можно that или when.

the reason — без слова, с that или с why: The reason I'm calling is to ask for your advice. = The reason why I'm calling…

grammar.title: 4. Добавка с запятыми: , who / , which
grammar.html:
У придаточного-«добавки» три жёстких правила — и все три противоположны тому, что вы учили в B1-21.
Какой именноДобавка
запятыенетда
thatможнонельзя
убрать словоможно (если не подлежащее)нельзя
  • John, who speaks four languages, works as a guide. — Джон, который говорит на четырёх языках, работает гидом.
  • Anna told me about her new job, which she's enjoying a lot.
  • We stayed at the Park Hotel, which a friend had recommended.
  • This morning I met Chris, who I hadn't seen for ages. (можно whom)
  • Kate has just been to Sweden, where her daughter lives.
  • Lisa, whose car had broken down, was in a terrible mood.
We played Hades, that I'd recommended to everyone.
We played Hades, which I'd recommended to everyone.

Запятая меняет смысл:

  • My sister who lives in Berlin is a designer. — у меня несколько сестёр, говорю о той, что в Берлине.
  • My sister, who lives in Berlin, is a designer. — сестра одна; «кстати, она в Берлине».

grammar.title: 5. Предлог + whom / which; all of whom, none of which
grammar.html:
В официальном английском предлог встаёт перед whom / which — прямо как в русском «с которым», «без которой». В разговоре предлог уходит в конец, и тогда whom не говорят.
ОфициальноРазговорно
Mr Lee, to whom I spoke yesterday, agreed.Mr Lee, who I spoke to yesterday, agreed.
the studio for which she worksthe studio she works for
  • Luckily we had a map, without which we would have got lost. — …без которой мы бы заблудились.
  • She works for a company called Nimbus, which I'd never heard of.
Mr Lee, to who I spoke, agreed.
Mr Lee, to whom I spoke, agreed. / Mr Lee, who I spoke to, agreed.

Число / часть + of whom (люди) / of which (вещи) — «из которых»:

  • Helen has three brothers, all of whom are married. — …все из которых женаты.
  • They asked me a lot of questions, most of which I couldn't answer.
  • I tried on three jackets, none of which fitted me.
  • Two men, neither of whom I'd seen before, walked into the office.
  • We have four monitors, two of which we never use.
  • We stayed in a lovely hotel, the name of which I've forgotten.
I have ten followers, most of them are bots.
I have ten followers, most of whom are bots. (или: …ten followers. Most of them are bots.)

grammar.title: 6. , which — про всю фразу целиком
grammar.html:
Иногда «что» относится не к одному слову, а к всему событию: «Джо получил работу, что всех удивило». По-английски тут только , which — и никогда не what.
целая фраза,which+комментарий
  • Joe got the job, which surprised everyone. — Джо получил работу, что всех удивило.
  • Sarah couldn't come, which was a shame. — Сара не смогла прийти, и это обидно.
  • The weather was great, which we hadn't expected. — Погода была отличная, чего мы не ожидали.
  • The patch deleted everyone's saves, which made the players furious.
  • He said he'd send the files by Monday, which means Wednesday. — …а это значит, в среду.
The server went down, what was annoying.
The server went down, which was annoying.
В живой речи , which is… — любимый способ добавить свою оценку: …which is fine, …which is crazy, …which is why I left.

grammar.title: 7. the woman talking to Tom, the game made by two people
grammar.html:
Придаточное можно сжать: убираем who is / that was — и остаётся -ing (активный смысл: сам делает) или 3-я форма (пассивный смысл: с ним сделали). В B2-5 -ing относился к действию; здесь он описывает существительное, как русское причастие «разговаривающий», «сделанный».
ПолностьюСжато
the woman who is talking to Tomthe woman talking to Tom
people who were waiting outsidepeople waiting outside
the boy who was injured in the accidentthe boy injured in the accident
a game that was made by two peoplea game made by two people

-ing — и для «прямо сейчас», и для «всегда»:

  • Police investigating the robbery want to talk to you. — Полиция, расследующая ограбление…
  • I was woken up by a dog barking. — Меня разбудил лай собаки.
  • The road connecting the two villages is very narrow. (всегда соединяет)
  • I have a room overlooking the park. — У меня комната с видом на парк.
  • Name a game beginning with Z.

3-я форма — пассивный смысл; помните про неправильные (stolen, made, built, written):

  • The money stolen in the robbery was never found.
  • Most of the phones made in this factory are exported.
  • He showed me some sketches drawn by his grandfather.

С there is / there was: There were some kids swimming in the river. · Is there anybody waiting? · There was a red car parked outside. А left = «оставшийся»: There's only one slice left.

The man was sitting next to me snored all flight.
The man sitting next to me snored all flight. / The man who was sitting…
A game making by two people.
A game made by two people. — игру сделали, она сама не делает

grammar.title: 8. Типичные ошибки — проверьте себя
grammar.html:
I have a colleague who's cat is on every call.
I have a colleague whose cat is on every call.
The town where I visited was tiny.
The town (that) I visited was tiny.
My mum that is a teacher lives in Tver.
My mum, who is a teacher, lives in Tver.
We watched Arcane, I loved.
We watched Arcane, which I loved.
She has two cats, both of them sleep all day.
She has two cats, both of which sleep all day.
The team won, what nobody expected.
The team won, which nobody expected.
The man to who I spoke…
The man I spoke to… / The man to whom I spoke…
The car stealing last night was found.
The car stolen last night was found.
Итог юнита в одной строке
whose + существительное · where = there · запятые = добавка: , who / , which, без that · all of whom / none of which · , which про всю фразу · the guy talking / the game made.

words: I met a girl whose dad is a pilot.
Я познакомился с девушкой, у которой папа — пилот.
The man to whom I spoke was very polite.
Человек, с которым я говорил, был очень вежлив.
She’s an artist whose work I really admire.
Это художница, чьей работой я искренне восхищаюсь.
This is the street where I grew up.
My hometown, which has only 20,000 people, has three cinemas.
В моём родном городе, где всего 20 000 жителей, три кинотеатра.
My flatmate, who works nights, sleeps all day.
Мой сосед по квартире, который работает по ночам, весь день спит.
The founder of the studio, whose first game failed, never gave up.
Основатель студии, чья первая игра провалилась, не сдался.
The game was launched in May, which was a mistake.
Игру выпустили в мае, и это было ошибкой.
He showed me his new app, of which he’s very proud.
Он показал мне своё новое приложение, которым очень гордится.
I share a desk with Oleg, who I get on really well with.
Я сижу за одним столом с Олегом, с которым отлично лажу.
The wedding, to which only family were invited, was lovely.
Свадьба, на которую пригласили только родных, была чудесной.
We got a room overlooking the sea.
Нам дали номер с видом на море.
The bridge connecting the two islands is closed.
It’s a village surrounded by mountains.
There was a fire, the cause of which is still unknown.
Был пожар, причина которого до сих пор неизвестна.
The houses damaged in the storm are being repaired.
The bike stolen from our yard was found.
Велосипед, украденный из нашего двора, нашли.
They hired two artists, both of whom are from Kazan.
Они наняли двух художников, оба из Казани.
Ten candidates applied, none of whom was suitable.
Подали заявки десять кандидатов, и ни один не подошёл.
We need a place where it’s quiet and suitable for recording.
Нам нужно тихое место, подходящее для записи.
The majority of people working here are under thirty.
Большинству людей, работающих здесь, нет тридцати.
I asked two friends, neither of whom knew the answer.
Я спросил двух друзей, и ни один не знал ответа.
There are only two tickets left.
There was a van parked outside my house.
He couldn’t come, which was a shame.
Он не смог прийти, и это обидно.
The ending, which was totally unexpected, made me cry.
Концовка, совершенно неожиданная, довела меня до слёз.
Fortunately, we had a map, without which we’d have got lost.
К счастью, у нас была карта, без которой мы бы заблудились.
The woman in charge of the project, whose name I forget, was great.
Женщина, руководившая проектом, чьё имя я забыл, была отличной.
The location where they filmed the series is in Scotland.
Место, где снимали сериал, находится в Шотландии.
I was woken up by a dog barking.

texts.title: The man who knew our kitchen
texts.text:
Last month our flatmate Pavel moved to Lisbon, which left Vera and me with an empty room, a big hole in our budget and a cactus that neither of us wanted to water.

The flat is in a great location. It overlooks a small park, it's well connected to the centre, and it's surrounded by cafés whose owners know our names. So when we posted an ad online, we got forty-three messages in a single day.

We invited nine people to see the room, all of whom promised to be “quiet, clean and friendly”. The majority of them were none of these things. The first candidate was a man whose first question was whether he could park his motorbike in the hallway. The second was a student who spent the whole visit filming our kitchen for his followers. Then came a woman whom we both liked immediately — until she mentioned her four cats, none of whom, she said, “really like people”.

By Sunday evening we were tired and a little desperate. Then the doorbell rang, and downstairs our neighbour's dog started barking, which it only does for postmen and serious events.

At the door stood a quiet man of about sixty holding a cake. His name was Lev. He explained that he had grown up in this building — in fact, in the very flat where we were standing — and that he had just come back to his hometown after thirty years in Canada.

“My mother's kitchen was right there,” he said, pointing at our fridge. “I did my homework at that window. Is the room still free?”

Fortunately, it was. Lev was easily the most suitable person we had met all week, which surprised nobody more than us. He gets on well with everyone, he repairs things that nobody else can repair, and he is now officially in charge of the cactus, which has never looked better.

There was only one unexpected moment. On his first evening, Lev noticed a loose board in the wall of his room. Behind it he found a small tin box, hidden there by a ten-year-old boy in 1975. Inside were three coins, a toy car and a note written in pencil: “Property of Lev. Do not touch.”

He laughed so hard that he had to sit down. It's a shame Pavel left before he could see it. He lived in that room for four years and never noticed a thing.

questions.q: Why did Vera and the narrator need a new flatmate?
What was the problem with the woman they both liked?
o: She wanted to park a motorbike in the hallway

questions.q: What did Lev find behind the loose board?
o: A box he had hidden there as a boy

texts.title: Choosing the new designer
texts.text:
Kate: OK, we have to decide today. Three candidates, one job. Who do you remember best?
Tim: The guy whose portfolio was all cats. Every single screen had a cat on it.
Kate: Arseny. He's the founder's nephew, by the way, which makes this a bit awkward.
Tim: Is he? That explains the confidence. He told me our app looks like a tax form from 2009.
Kate: Well, he isn't completely wrong. Who else?
Tim: The woman who used to work for a bank. Nadia? The one whose cover letter was four pages long.
Kate: Yes. Very experienced, very serious. She asked who would be in charge of approving her holidays before she asked a single question about the product.
Tim: Perfect for a bank. Not so suitable for us. And the third one was the quiet guy sitting in the corner before the interview, eating an apple?
Kate: Mark. The one we almost forgot to invite. His CV landed in the spam folder, which is a shame, because his test task was the best one we got.
Tim: Remind me what he did.
Kate: He redesigned our booking screen, the one causing all the complaints. Neither of the other candidates even noticed it was broken.
Tim: Wait. The booking screen that I designed?
Kate: That very screen.
Tim: I suddenly like Mark a lot less.
Kate: Come on, he was very polite about it. Listen: “The original designer, whom I admire, clearly had very little time.”
Tim: That's actually true. They gave me two days. Fine. And the rest of the team?
Kate: Lena and Max, both of whom saw all three test tasks, voted for Mark. Arseny got one vote.
Tim: From whom?
Kate: From his uncle.
Tim: Of course. So what do we do about the founder?
Kate: I've already spoken to him. He only voted for Arseny because his sister asked him to. Fortunately, he hates the cat screens more than anyone. He said a portfolio made by someone with that much free time worries him.
Tim: So it's Mark. Shall I call him?
Kate: Already done. He starts on Monday. And Tim, the first task he's getting is the booking screen. With you. Try to get on with him.
Tim: I'll be nice, I promise. I'll even bring him an apple.

questions.q: Why is the situation with Arseny awkward?
o: He was late for the interview

questions.q: Whose booking screen did Mark redesign?

practice.q: I follow a streamer ___ dog always steals the show.
I have a cousin ___ just moved to Canada.
practice.why: who's = who has: who has just moved.

practice.q: That's the hospital ___ I was born.
practice.why: I was born there — место → where.

practice.q: Our designer, ___ lives in Minsk, works remotely.
practice.why: Добавка с запятыми: that нельзя, слово нельзя пропустить → who.

practice.q: Our team missed the deadline, ___ made the client angry.
She has three sisters, ___ are older than her.
practice.why: Люди + «из которых» внутри одного предложения → of whom.

practice.q: Who's the woman ___ to your boss?
practice.why: Сжатое придаточное: the woman (who is) talking — сама говорит → -ing.

practice.q: Most of the furniture ___ in this factory is sold abroad.
The reason ___ I left early is simple: I was exhausted. (почему)
a: why
that
practice.why: После the reason можно why, that или ничего.

practice.q: Mr Park, to ___ I sent the invoice, hasn't replied. (которому)
a: whom
practice.why: Предлог перед словом о человеке → только whom.

practice.q: He bought three games, none of ___ he has played. (которых)
a: which
practice.why: Вещи + none of → none of which.

a: left
practice.why: left = оставшийся: there's only one left.

practice.q: The police found the car ___ last week. (steal)
a: stolen

practice.q: I have a room ___ the garden. (overlook)
a: overlooking

practice.ru: Я вернулся в город, где вырос

practice.a: The man sitting next to me snored
practice.ru: Мужчина, сидевший рядом со мной, храпел

test.q: I met a man ___ sister works with you.
The city ___ we visited last summer was beautiful.
test.why: visit что? it — не место «где», поэтому that (или ничего), а не where.

o: My dad, that is a doctor, works nights.
My dad, who is a doctor, works nights.
My dad who is a doctor works nights.
test.why: Папа один → добавка с запятыми и who, that нельзя.

test.q: We stayed at the Grand Hotel, ___ a friend had recommended. (который)
a: which
test.why: Добавка с запятой → which; убрать слово или поставить that нельзя.

test.q: Kate showed me photos of her son, of ___ she's very proud.
test.why: Предлог перед словом о человеке → whom.

test.q: Какое предложение звучит естественно в разговоре?
o: The guy whom I was talking to
The guy I was talking to
The guy to who I was talking
test.why: В разговоре слово опускают, а предлог ставят в конец. whom в разговоре звучит книжно, а после предлога нужен whom, не who.

test.q: Ten people applied for the job, ___ of whom had any experience. (ни один)
a: none
test.why: none of whom = ни один из которых.

test.q: The patch fixed nothing, ___ was really annoying.
test.why: , which относится ко всей фразе; what здесь невозможен.

test.q: That's the day ___ we got married. (когда)
a: when
that
test.why: После the day — when, that или ничего.

test.q: Police ___ the crime are looking for two men.
test.why: Полиция сама расследует → -ing clause без who is.

test.q: The boy ___ in the accident is in hospital. (injure)
a: injured

test.q: There was a strange car ___ outside our house all night.
test.why: Машина припаркована (с ней это сделали) → there was + 3-я форма.
